title: The Ordinary Path and the Special Path
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Master Yinguang instructed: “The methods of practice are of two kinds. If one relies on one’s own power to cultivate precepts, concentration, and wisdom, until reaching the extinction of delusions (the delusions of views and thoughts) and realizing truth, and so ends birth and death—this is called the ordinary path. If one possesses true faith and a sincere vow, holds the Buddha’s name, and hopes by the Buddha’s compassionate power to be reborn in the West—this is called the special path.”

their own power—for example, Chan meditation: through investigating the huatou one brings the myriad thoughts back to one (single-minded undividedness), then the one back to nothing (no single thought arising), then illuminates the mind and sees the nature (clearly seeing the original nature), and only then, through maintaining this and dispersing habits, eradicates the delusions of views and thoughts and ends birth and death. Another example is mind-contemplation: through contemplating the flow of karmic consciousness within one’s own mind one reaches no-thought-arising, illuminates the mind and sees the nature, and only then, through maintaining this and dispersing habits, eradicates the delusions and ends birth and death.

[The delusions of views and thoughts: the delusion of views and the delusion of thought. The delusion of views is the confusion of ordinary people in their views, such as the five false views of self-view, extreme-view, heterodox-view, view-attachment, and precept-and-practice-attachment. The delusion of thought is the confusion of ordinary people in their thoughts, such as the afflictions of greed, anger, delusion, arrogance, and doubt. These two delusions are the root of sentient beings falling into the three realms and suffering birth and death in vain; eradicating them enables one to end birth and death and escape the cycle.]
Both the Chan school’s Chan meditation and mind-contemplation require eradicating the delusions of views and thoughts before one can end birth and death; this is entirely relying on
